subject: NeonCommerce launch: in‑flight quota coordination and temporary fallback routing
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@neoncommerce.com>, Joe Park <joe.park@cloudops.neoncommerce.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NeonCommerce launch: request for temporary throughput uplift and fallback

Team / Neon,

Quick summary: NeonCommerce will open their new checkout feature to ~10% of traffic on Thu Jul 4 and we expect an initial burst that could exceed their current quota by ~2.2x for a 48–72 hour window. They asked for an emergency runway so the feature doesn't hit 429s during the holiday.

Ask: Can infra/product approve a temporary quota uplift (2x baseline tokens/sec) for the window 2028-07-04 00:00 UTC → 2028-07-06 23:59 UTC and a routing fallback to the smaller model variant if error rate climbs above 3%?

What I attached: neon_launch_72hr_forecast.xlsx — per-minute TPS projections by endpoint, and a draft SLA/exception doc (neon_sla-exception_draft.pdf).

Notes / constraints:
- Neon will not accept degraded accuracy beyond minor fallback (we can route low-latency requests to gpt-2-small variant for non-critical calls).
- Procurement is pushing to finalize commercial language this week; Marissa, I copied you for contract timing.
- We prefer a short-lived uplift rather than permanent quota change.

If product needs shape of the spike or endpoint names, I can paste that below — Connor

--
Connor O'Brien
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@neoncommerce.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeonCommerce launch: request for temporary throughput uplift and fallback

Thanks Connor — useful context. A few clarifying questions before I sign off: 

1) Spike shape: is the 2.2x a flat multiplier across all endpoints or concentrated on the /checkout/generate and /checkout/confirm routes?
2) Which models/endpoints are they using today (model ids + max tokens)? That determines whether the fallback to a "small" variant is compatible.
3) Can they tolerate per-request latency increases up to ~150ms p95 if it prevents 429s?

From product POV, temporary uplift is doable if we get concrete per-endpoint TPS curves and a fallback plan that keeps output semantics (no hallucination regressions). Can you paste the per-minute slices? Also cc'ing Neha for runbook input.

Irene
Director, Product 
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, procurement@neoncommerce.com
Date: Fri, 24 Jun 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeonCommerce launch: request for temporary throughput uplift and fallback

Looping in procurement and reiterating our timeline constraints. Neon needs the uplift confirmed so they can finalize the traffic-exposure plan with their PM (Sarah). Procurement, can you confirm whether an SLA carveout for this 72h window is acceptable, or do we need an addendum? I attached the draft SLA exception (neon_sla-exception_draft.pdf) — it flags liability and outage language.

Also, quick commercial ask: if we approve uplift and a routing fallback, can we add a temporary uplift fee (one-time) to cover burst capacity? I'll coordinate pricing with finance once we know the uplift duration. Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@neoncommerce.com>, Joe Park <joe.park@cloudops.neoncommerce.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jun 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeonCommerce launch: request for temporary throughput uplift and fallback

Thanks — attached is a short canary-runbook.md with a staged ramp suggestion. High level:

- Run a 10% exposure for 4 hours, monitor 429s + p95 latency + top-5 error codes.
- If healthy, step to 30% for 6 hours, then 60% for 12 hours, then full 100% of the planned cohort.
- Permanent fallback: route to gpt-small for non-critical endpoints if 429 > 1% for 15m.

Practically, I'd recommend we:
- Approve the uplift for 72 hours but gate it on the canary checkpoints above.
- Configure an automatic rollback to baseline if error-rate or DB throttles appear.

Neha
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@neoncommerce.com>, Joe Park <joe.park@cloudops.neoncommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jun 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeonCommerce launch: request for temporary throughput uplift and fallback

Appended: per-endpoint slices from the spreadsheet (excerpt):
- /checkout/generate: baseline 120 req/min → peak 290 req/min (12:00–14:00 UTC window on day 1)
- /checkout/confirm: baseline 60 req/min → peak 140 req/min (same window)
- /catalog/recommend: baseline 200 req/min → peak 220 req/min (less critical)

Model details: production uses model id: redwood-gpt-4lite v2 (max tokens 1024). Fallback candidate: redwood-gpt-4lite-small (quantized, ~30% cost savings) — outputs differ slightly on chit-chat but not on semantic confirmations we need for checkout.

HubSpot deal (NEON-2028-P1) has procurement queued; they asked us for a technical signoff by EOD Mon Jul 1st so they can greenlight their QA run on Jul 2. Link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/NEON-2028-P1

Connor

> 2) Which models/endpoints are they using today (model ids + max tokens)? That determines whether the fallback to a "small" variant is compatible.
> 3) Can they tolerate per-request latency increases up to ~150ms p95 if it prevents 429s?

> Irene
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@neoncommerce.com>, Joe Park <joe.park@cloudops.neoncommerce.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeonCommerce launch: request for temporary throughput uplift and fallback — APPROVED (72h window)

Approvals: 
- Product (Irene): acknowledged the shape and fallback compatibility.
- Infra/Capacity: approved temporary uplift of 2x baseline tokens/sec for the window 2028-07-04 00:00 UTC → 2028-07-06 23:59 UTC, gated on Neha's canary checkpoints.

Operational notes / actions for runbook:
1) T+0: apply uplift and enable cost-metering tag (neon-ci/neon-boost).
2) Configure automatic fallback rule: route to redwood-gpt-4lite-small if 429 > 3% across /checkout/* for >=15m.
3) On-canary metrics dashboard (link posted in Drive), set alerts for 429 rate, p95 latency, error-distribution.
4) Post-mortem: runbook requires a short writeup within 48h after end of uplift window.

Attachments: canary-runbook.md (finalized), neon_sla-exception_draft.pdf (please review procurement language).

I'll schedule a 30-min dry-run on Wed Jul 3 at 1400 PDT to confirm the automation and alerts. Connor/Marissa — please bring Neon PM (Sarah) if possible.

Thanks — Tessa
Senior Capacity Planner
Redwood Inference
